docket.challenge_claim: The no-internal-seam warrant is falsified by the bytes the row itself quotes, a sustained singular address to Yahweh interrupting the plural addressees; the same warrant assigns the whole span to one speaker's mouth that the bytes contradict; and the Aramaic island's opening verb is mislabelled an imperative.
docket.grounds: The item stands. Form class: כִּדְנָה֙ תֵּאמְר֣וּן at oshb:Jer.10.11 = web:Jer.10.11 (byte tier, Aramaic) carries the tav prefix and the paragogic nun of a prefix-conjugation form, and the translation renders it as a modal future, “You shall say this to them” (web:Jer.10.11); no morphology layer is staged, so the label stands or falls on the pointed bytes plus the two renderings, and neither supports 'citation imperative'. That label is also the sharper locus of the contradiction the item names, since the same rationale asserts that no additional discourse imperative interrupts the span while calling this form one: correcting the form class cures both at a single edit. Frame ownership: the row places the mockery in one mouth on the strength of the onset formula at oshb:Jer.10.2 (byte tier), but the span carries at least two further speaker positions the bytes will not put in that mouth -- second-person praise addressed TO Yahweh at oshb:Jer.10.6, גָּד֥וֹל אַתָּ֛ה וְגָד֥וֹל שִׁמְךָ֖ (byte tier), continued at oshb:Jer.10.7, and third-person predication ABOUT Yahweh at oshb:Jer.10.10, וַֽיהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ אֱמֶ֔ת (byte tier). A koh-amar claim that does not name which mouth carries which stretch is the one claim this book's formula census will not support. One qualification on the addressee half: the rationale DOES disclose the praise turn before denying an 'additional' one, so this is a self-contradictory criterion rather than a suppressed fact -- still a defect, and the return to the plural addressees at oshb:Jer.10.11 is a further undisclosed turn. The holding is not disturbed: a thematic register alternation is not a tier-1 seam, the default for frame-plus-speech is the larger unit, and the island disclosure is present and correct (inventory: 15 Aramaic-coded morphs, all in that one verse). NEW, raised by neither lens: observed_substrate_signals files the hear-the-word plural imperative of oshb:Jer.10.1 (byte tier) under a word-event key, although the word-event system is a closed set of three shapes that are never blended and a discourse-frame imperative is not one of them; across the book's candidate rows the discourse-imperative signal element appears in 31 oss entries, 28 of them under narrative_frame or speech_formula keys and 3 under a word-event key. Second new item: device_notes places the seg at oshb:Jer.10.11 'inside the span', where under the follow-the-verse keying it stands at the span's CLOSING seam.
docket.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: re-label the Aramaic opener at oshb:Jer.10.11 = web:Jer.10.11 as a prefix-conjugation (modal) form, not an imperative, and re-read the criterion sentence so it no longer denies a signal the same sentence names. (2) boundary_rationale: name the mouth per stretch -- the formula-owned mockery, the second-person praise at oshb:Jer.10.6-Jer.10.7, the third-person predication at oshb:Jer.10.10, and the return to the plural addressees at oshb:Jer.10.11 -- or restate the warrant to claim only that no fresh divine-speech formula, addressee-naming imperative or discourse frame opens a rival unit inside the span. No respan is ordered: the span stands. (3) observed_substrate_signals: re-file the oshb:Jer.10.1 discourse imperative out of the word_event family into the key family the corpus uses for that class, and carry the same order as its own sweep to every row whose oss carries word_event.discourse_imperative_onset (P04-001, P04-003, P04-008). oss is a dependent field, so re-check confidence and strongest_rejected_alternative after the edit. (4) device_notes: state the oshb:Jer.10.11 seg as standing at the closing seam, not inside the span. TESTS the cure must pass: every form-class label in the row is readable off the pointed bytes plus both renderings -- the read that killed the original; no sentence denies a signal the same row names; every koh-amar claim names whose mouth carries which verses; and the oss key set contains no word-event key that is not one of the three attested word-event shapes.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The unit opens on a plural summons, שִׁמְע֣וּ אֶת הַדָּבָ֗ר (oshb:Jer.10.1, byte), matching “Hear the word which Yahweh speaks to you, house of Israel!” (web:Jer.10.1). A koh-amar onset follows at once, כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.10.2, byte), placing the idol mockery of the surrounding verses in Yahweh's own mouth rather than the prophet's. A doxological interjection breaks in mid-polemic, מֵאֵ֥ין כָּמ֖וֹךָ יְהוָ֑ה גָּד֥וֹל (oshb:Jer.10.6, byte) — praise addressed directly to Yahweh — so that idol mockery and praise alternate through the same speech rather than sitting in separate blocks; no additional koh-amar, addressee shift, or discourse imperative interrupts that alternation, so it is read here as one unit rather than divided at these internal turns. It closes on an Aramaic sentence, כִּדְנָה֙ תֵּאמְר֣וּן לְה֔וֹם אֱלָ֣הַיָּ֔א דִּֽי שְׁמַיָּ֥א וְאַרְקָ֖א לָ֣א עֲבַ֑דוּ (oshb:Jer.10.11, byte) — “You shall say this to them: ‘The gods that have not made the heavens and the earth will perish from the earth, and from under the heavens.’” (web:Jer.10.11) — a self-contained Aramaic island inside the surrounding Hebrew, functioning as the refutation formula Israel is told to hand back to the nations; the citation imperative that opens it belongs with the preceding mockery, and the row is cut here because verse 12 opens a distinct hymnic unit in Hebrew rather than continuing this address.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the praise interjections from the surrounding idol mockery into their own row was rejected because no koh-amar onset, addressee shift, or discourse imperative marks a fresh seam between them; the two registers interleave inside the same divine speech.

docket.challenge_claim: The twin cross-reference is an untiered recurrence claim that the consonantal evidence bears only in part, and the ketiv/qere note is argued from an English rendering that cannot register the variant.
docket.grounds: Both halves check out on the bytes. The narrow claim is exact: יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ closes oshb:Jer.10.16 and the identical run closes oshb:Jer.51.19 (byte tier, both). The wider designation is not: of the five verse pairs, two are byte-identical (oshb:Jer.10.12 against oshb:Jer.51.15; oshb:Jer.10.15 against oshb:Jer.51.18) and three diverge already at skeleton tier -- oshb:Jer.10.13 carries the ketiv/qere doublet where oshb:Jer.51.16 has a single article-less noun, besides two divergent verb forms; oshb:Jer.10.14 carries the refiner noun plene against the defective spelling at oshb:Jer.51.17; and oshb:Jer.10.16 has the defective Jacob noun with an Israel noun before the tribe noun against the plene Jacob and no Israel noun at oshb:Jer.51.19. No tier is named anywhere on the recurrence claim, where campaign practice requires one on every recurrence sentence, so which of these the row asserts cannot be read off it. The ketiv/qere inference is falsified by the witnesses themselves. The note is inventory-true and both forms stand in the source bytes, מִקְצֵ֣ה ארץ הָאָ֑רֶץ at oshb:Jer.10.13. But the parallel verse carries the article-less מִקְצֵה אָ֑רֶץ at oshb:Jer.51.16 (byte tier), and the translation renders the two identically -- “from the ends of the earth” (web:Jer.10.13) and “from the ends of the earth” (web:Jer.51.16) -- so the English cannot register the article and is evidence for neither reading. A witness-internal variant is never adjudicated from a translation. The row's edges are unaffected: the participial opening is verse-initial at oshb:Jer.10.12 and the name-formula verse-final at oshb:Jer.10.16 (byte tier, both), and the seg keyed after oshb:Jer.10.11 stands at the front seam exactly as the row says (parashah tier-3, single-witness).
docket.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale and device_notes: tier-label the recurrence and scope it -- the closing name-formula is byte-identical at oshb:Jer.10.16 and oshb:Jer.51.19; if the wider pairing is kept as texture, state the tier at which it holds and that three of the five verse pairs diverge in the consonants. (2) device_notes: delete the inference that the qere supplies the definite reading carried into the English; the same English stands over the article-less parallel at oshb:Jer.51.16 = web:Jer.51.16. Retain the note as a single-witness disclosure of the two forms with no reading preferred. TESTS the cure must pass: every recurrence sentence names its tier and the extent it claims, and survives a byte comparison of all five verse pairs -- the comparison that killed the original; and no ketiv/qere, parashah or other witness-internal claim anywhere in the row is argued from an English rendering.

docket.challenge_claim: The unqualified statement that nothing before this verse addresses Yahweh in the second person is refuted by the bytes seventeen verses earlier in the same chapter, and the exclusivity is asserted without a swept object or a sweep count.
docket.grounds: The clause is false as written. oshb:Jer.10.6 reads כָּמ֖וֹךָ יְהוָ֑ה גָּד֥וֹל אַתָּ֛ה וְגָד֥וֹל שִׁמְךָ֖ and oshb:Jer.10.7 opens מִ֣י לֹ֤א יִֽרָאֲךָ֙ (byte tier, both): a second-person masculine independent pronoun, second-person suffixes on the name-noun and the preposition, and a second-person verbal object, and both witnesses render them as address rather than description -- “There is no one like you, Yahweh. You are great, and your name is great in might.” (web:Jer.10.6). Those verses stand seventeen verses before the row's onset, inside the row's own chapter and inside the same parent frame, so the stated front-seam discriminator does not survive its own chapter. The claim is separately defective as an exclusivity: a first/nothing-before assertion carries an adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming the swept object and the unit, and is never softened by a tier label; neither is present. The boundary is not in question and the item does not ask for one: a seg follows oshb:Jer.10.22 -- at the front seam under the follow-the-verse keying (parashah tier-3, single-witness) -- and the turn into first-person petition addressed to Yahweh at oshb:Jer.10.23, יָדַ֣עְתִּי יְהוָ֔ה (byte tier), carried on by the second-person imperatives of oshb:Jer.10.24-Jer.10.25, is a speaker-role and addressee change in its own right. The defect lies in the warrant, not in the edge.
docket.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: delete the first-occurrence clause and rest the front-seam warrant on the change it can actually carry -- the turn out of third-person report of the northern rumour at oshb:Jer.10.22 into first-person petition addressed to Yahweh from oshb:Jer.10.23, with the splice and tier already in the field. (2) If any first / only / nothing-before claim is retained anywhere in the row, attach an adjacent sweep digit naming the swept object (second-person address to Yahweh) and the unit (verses), and state its scope explicitly. TESTS the cure must pass: the replacement warrant must survive a read of oshb:Jer.10.6-Jer.10.7 -- the read that killed the original -- and no universal or exclusivity claim may stand in any field without an in-sentence digit naming its object and unit.

docket.challenge_claim: The opening header is byte-perfect, but two byte-true catchwords cross this unit's closing seam undisclosed, the recurrence claim to the earlier header site carries no tier where one is owed, and confidence is set at high with the frontier flag unset.
docket.grounds: Both straddles verify. שִׁמְע֕וּ אֶת דִּבְרֵ֖י הַבְּרִ֣ית הַזֹּ֑את stands at oshb:Jer.11.2 inside the span and recurs beyond the cut at oshb:Jer.11.6 as שִׁמְע֗וּ אֶת דִּבְרֵי֙ הַבְּרִ֣ית הַזֹּ֔את -- skeleton-identical, not byte-identical -- and those are the only two verses in the book carrying the run (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier). The summons שִׁמְע֤וּ בְקוֹלִי֙ at oshb:Jer.11.4 recurs beyond the cut at oshb:Jer.11.7 as שִׁמְע֖וּ בְּקוֹלִֽי, again skeleton-identical only (sweep: 4 verses, skeleton tier). The counter-reading that this is ordinary sermon vocabulary rather than a device fails on the digit: a clause attested in exactly two verses book-wide is not ordinary vocabulary, and the disclosure duty does not depend on whether the device defeats the cut. The cut itself survives and should be said to survive: the fresh narrative reintroduction at oshb:Jer.11.6, וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י (byte tier; sweep: 13 verses, skeleton tier), reopens address after the prophet's own reply closes the exchange at oshb:Jer.11.5, and a seg follows oshb:Jer.11.5 at that seam (parashah tier-3, single-witness). One qualification: the confidence setting is not an independent defect. confidence and frontier_flag_considered are dependent on the disclosure repair and are re-set after it, not found against on their own; the hard whole-chapter cap arm binds chapter-length spans, and this five-verse span is not one.
docket.remedy: (1) device_notes (or boundary_rationale): disclose both straddling runs by verse and tier -- the covenant-words summons at oshb:Jer.11.2 recurring at oshb:Jer.11.6 (skeleton tier; sweep: 2 verses) and the obey-my-voice summons at oshb:Jer.11.4 recurring at oshb:Jer.11.7 (skeleton tier; sweep: 4 verses) -- and state why they do not carry the unit across the seam: the reintroduction at oshb:Jer.11.6 reopens address after the reply at oshb:Jer.11.5. (2) boundary_rationale: tier-label the header recurrence as byte-identical to oshb:Jer.7.1 across the whole verse, with the family digit attached (sweep: 11 verses). (3) confidence and frontier_flag_considered: re-assess as dependent fields once (1) and (2) land. No boundary change is ordered. TESTS the cure must pass: the repaired row names every byte-true run that straddles either of its own seams, with the tier at which each matches; every recurrence sentence carries a tier and a digit; and the closing warrant must still stand with the straddling pair on the page -- the test the original never faced.

docket.challenge_claim: The discriminator separating this unit from what precedes — a turn to the present generation's conspiracy rather than the fathers' history just recalled — is contradicted by this unit's own second verse, which names the forefathers twice; and the speech formula at MT 11:11, on which the refusal to cut turns, is left unspliced.
docket.grounds: The formula limb is upheld and the contrast limb needs correction. B2-1.grounds: Re-derived from the pointed bytes. The seam the merge would delete carries a ruled tier-1 class. Jer.12.1-Jer.12.4 addresses the deity by name, צַדִּ֤יק אַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.12.1, byte tier) and וְאַתָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ יְדַעְתָּ֔נִי (oshb:Jer.12.3, byte tier), while 12:5 turns the second person onto the prophet, כִּ֣י אֶת רַגְלִ֥ים רַ֨צְתָּה֙ וַיַּלְא֔וּךָ (oshb:Jer.12.5, byte tier), and 12:6 brings a participant set standing nowhere in 12:1-12:4, אַחֶ֣יךָ וּבֵית אָבִ֗יךָ (oshb:Jer.12.6, byte tier). An explicit addressee-and-participant shift is a licensed tier-1 internal seam, so the cut survives on the ground the challenge itself supplies, not on the ground the row argues. The remaining arms verify. No messenger formula stands between the seam and either neighbour: the consonantal formula object returns 152 verses book-wide at MT keys with its nearest members at MT 11:22 and MT 12:14 and none between (sweep: 152 verses). The first person at 12:1 resumes the voice already standing at הֽוֹדִיעַ֖נִי וָֽאֵדָ֑עָה (oshb:Jer.11.18, byte tier) and גִּלִּ֥יתִי אֶת רִיבִֽי (oshb:Jer.11.20, byte tier) across the reply of 11:21-11:23, so the new-first-person-voice warrant is byte-false as charged. The treachery catchword straddling the seam is a disclosure obligation under the cross-seam cohesion rule, which a disclosure cures; it is not a seam-deleter. COUNT OBJECT CORRECTED, controlling object and digit pair named: the docket's 12-verse figure is a bare consonantal substring that blends three bases, the treachery family, the garment noun at MT 36:24, MT 41:5 and MT 52:33, and a bet-prefixed noun at MT 49:3, so it may not be cited as the treachery family's count. The controlling objects are the attested forms: בֹּ֥גְדֵי (oshb:Jer.12.1, byte tier) returns 1 verse at byte and at accent-stripped tier, and בָּ֣גְדוּ (oshb:Jer.12.6, byte tier) returns 1 verse at byte tier and 2 at accent-stripped tier (MT 5:11 and MT 12:6). current_row.boundary_rationale: The addressee turns around without any introducing formula: כִּ֣י אֶת רַגְלִ֥ים רַ֨צְתָּה֙ וַיַּלְא֔וּךָ (oshb:Jer.12.5, byte), matching “If you have run with the footmen, and they have wearied you, then how can you contend with horses?” (web:Jer.12.5), reads as Yahweh's own reply to the complaint just voiced, now naming Jeremiah as the one addressed rather than the one speaking. The reply closes with a warning against Jeremiah's own household, אַל תַּאֲמֵ֣ן בָּ֔ם (oshb:Jer.12.6, byte) — “Don’t believe them, though they speak beautiful words to you.” (web:Jer.12.6). docket.challenge_claim: That the one-unit warrant's claim that no addressee change and no discourse imperative interrupts 12:7-13 is falsified by the span's own bytes at two verses -- the plural imperatives of 12:9 and the second-person plural suffix at 12:13.
docket.grounds: The defect is real; one arm of its framing is not. Byte-true: oshb:Jer.12.9 carries לְכ֗וּ אִסְפ֛וּ together with הֵתָ֥יוּ (byte; that imperative pair, sweep: 1 verse), so an unqualified denial that any discourse imperative interrupts the span is false at the token level, and the feature goes undisclosed. Byte-true: וּבֹ֨שׁוּ֙ מִתְּבוּאֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם at oshb:Jer.12.13 (byte) carries a second-person masculine plural suffix and turns the speech to the addressed people, a party other than the summoned agents of 12:9 -- likewise undisclosed, and it does contradict the no-addressee-change arm as written. Byte-false: calling 12:13 the span's FIRST direct second-person address does not hold, since the 12:9 imperatives are themselves second-person forms standing four verses earlier; an ordinal of that kind needs its own digit-bearing sweep of the named object and does not survive one. The koh-amar arm holds: nearest sites are 11:22 before and 12:14 after (sweep: 152 verses), none between. The one-unit result also survives: the 12:9 imperatives summon the field's creatures inside the poem's own imagery rather than opening a fresh commission to an audience -- the class this row treats as a seam at 13:15 and 13:18 -- and 12:13 carries no fresh discourse frame. What fails is the unqualified wording and the missing disclosure, not the boundary.
docket.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the unqualified three-part denial with a qualified statement naming both in-span features and why neither is a seam of the ruled classes -- the plural imperatives at 12:9 summoning agents inside the poem's imagery, and the second-person plural suffix at 12:13 turning to the addressed people without a fresh discourse frame; keep the koh-amar arm, which the census supports. device_notes: disclose both features with swept object and verse count. Test the cure must pass: no absolute absence claim stands where the span's own bytes carry a token of the named class, and any first/only/sole ordinal carries an adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming the swept object and unit.

docket.challenge_claim: That both frame warrants pair a byte-tier Hebrew splice with English rendering different words of the same verse, so neither the onset formula nor the closure formula is glossed by the text offered as its match; and that the verse's single count-only seg is undisclosed.
docket.grounds: Both pairings are broken on the bytes. At 12:14 the other witness renders the formula verse-initially as “Yahweh says,” (web:Jer.12.14), while the spliced כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.12.14, byte) is paired with the plucking-up clause, which renders הִנְנִ֤י נֹֽתְשָׁם֙ מֵעַ֣ל אַדְמָתָ֔ם (oshb:Jer.12.14, byte) -- a different stretch of the same verse. At 12:17 the other witness renders the formula verse-finally as “says Yahweh.” (web:Jer.12.17), while the spliced נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.12.17, byte) is paired with the clause preceding it and that English omits the formula's own rendering altogether, inverting the pairing. Gloss extent must equal splice extent; neither pairing meets it. The substantive reading survives: נְאֻם יְהוָֽה is verse-final at oshb:Jer.12.17 (byte), and a fresh private commission opens at oshb:Jer.13.1 with כֹּֽה אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י (byte; that shape, sweep: 3 verses), so the closure corroboration is correctly placed under the closure-only handling this formula carries at its book-wide density. The count-only seg at MT 12:14 is inventory-true but position-free and outside the unconditional paragraph-mark symmetry arm -- a low-weight completeness point that does not lift severity.
docket.remedy: boundary_rationale: re-pair both matches -- pair the koh-amar splice with the WEB rendering “Yahweh says,” (web:Jer.12.14) and the neum splice with “says Yahweh.” (web:Jer.12.17); if the plucking-up English is retained, splice the clause it renders beside it. device_notes: record the single count-only seg at oshb:Jer.12.14 as single-witness with no position claim. Test the cure must pass: each curly-quoted WEB run renders exactly the Hebrew spliced beside it, verified against both witnesses' bytes at the same verse, with the formula's own rendering never omitted from the pairing that carries it.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A koh-amar clause turns the address outward to the neighboring nations, כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.12.14, byte), matching “Behold, I will pluck them up from off their land,” (web:Jer.12.14), naming those who touch the heritage just lamented rather than the heritage itself. A promise of compassion for Jacob and a conditional blessing for the neighbors who learn Jacob's ways are folded into the same speech rather than opening fresh units of their own — an operative judgment-oracle reading is kept for the whole four verses, with the restoration content disclosed here rather than given a separate label, since the unit opens and closes on uprooting language and the compassion clause is grammatically subordinate to it. The unit, and the chapter, close on the closing-speech formula, נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.12.17, byte), matching “But if they will not hear, then I will pluck up that nation, plucking up and destroying it,” (web:Jer.12.17); a fresh command opens immediately afterward at web:Jer.13.1, corroborating the close read here.
